exercises.name: Known hash and candidates
exercises.action: Create a scratch directory; put the hash on one line in hash.txt and the three words on separate lines in words.txt. Run hashcat -m 0 -a 0 --potfile-disable hash.txt words.txt; expected recovered plaintext password. Optional John: john --format=raw-md5 --wordlist=words.txt --pot=toy.pot hash.txt, then john --format=raw-md5 --show --pot=toy.pot hash.txt. Use a fresh scratch directory to avoid stale pot results.
exercises.expected: password is the matching candidate; adding only digits would never find it. A mask password?d tries ten different strings, none equal to password.
exercises.fallback: Python: import hashlib; words=["dragon","password","letmein"]; print([w for w in words if hashlib.md5(w.encode()).hexdigest()=="5f4dcc3b5aa765d61d8327deb882cf99"]). Expected ["password"].
exercises.validation: Expected MD5 computed and asserted in Python; hashcat/John commands not executed and backend availability unknown.

exercises.name: Archive classification without a download
exercises.action: Choose the member whose plaintext is directly usable and explain why. Write the exact prefix to plain.txt without a newline, name the bkcrack -C/-c/-p arguments, and explain why an internal key is enough to recover content. No archive needed for this recall check.
exercises.expected: Choose spiral.svg because it is stored; prefix is 20 bytes. With the upstream secrets.zip: bkcrack -C secrets.zip -c spiral.svg -p plain.txt. Tutorial’s keys are c4490e28 b414a23d 91404b31; these enable password removal. Do not infer those keys for other archives.

exercises.name: Tiny local archive sanity check
exercises.input: note.txt containing exactly flag{offline} followed by a newline (14 bytes).
exercises.action: Python in a fresh scratch directory: import zipfile; z=zipfile.ZipFile("toy.zip","w",compression=zipfile.ZIP_STORED); z.writestr("note.txt",b"flag{offline}\n"); z.close(). Reopen with zipfile.ZipFile("toy.zip"), inspect getinfo("note.txt").flag_bits & 1 and compress_type, then read("note.txt").
exercises.expected: Encryption bit 0, compression type 0, plaintext b"flag{offline}\n". No bkcrack attack is needed.
exercises.fallback: If no interpreter is available, classify the given flags (0) and method (0) on paper.
exercises.validation: Equivalent in-memory Python ZIP creation, flags, compression and readback executed and asserted; no external archive binary tested.

factordb-python is network-dependent and unnecessary for the tiny local RSA fixture. Keep reference only; approval is not authorization to transmit event challenge material.

hlextend and padding-oracle-attacker are pattern-specific helpers needing a vulnerable construction/oracle. General RSA/hash exercises do not cover them; retain exact upstream references and state this gap instead of claiming broad cryptographic mastery.
PARI/GP is an alternative number-theory runtime; Sage/Python cover this block’s arithmetic. Use the existing reference if a supplied solver specifically needs GP.
hashid is triage, not proof of algorithm identity; check context and known format examples before selecting a cracking mode.
rockyou is a wordlist, not a separate tool course. The three-word fixture teaches candidate handling without downloading a large corpus.
OpenSSL remains reference-only for explicit cipher, key, IV and salt parameters; the curated block does not claim AES/OpenSSL coverage.
multimon-ng signal decoding needs an appropriate recorded signal and modulation knowledge; reference-only pending a matching challenge, not covered by the crypto refresh.
